subject: Cognitive Science
title: Spaced Repetition
description: A quick, practical guide to Spaced Repetition.

hook.text: Cram the night before and it's gone by Monday. Space the same study over days? It lasts for months.

buildup.text: Ebbinghaus discovered in 1885 that distributed practice beats massed practice—every time.

discovery.text: Each retrieval at the edge of forgetting strengthens the memory trace and resets the decay clock.

twist.text: Spacing feels harder than cramming. Students rate it as worse—but their test scores say otherwise.

climax.text: Flashcard apps like Anki automate this: showing cards just before you'd forget them.

punchline.text: Spread out, dig in. That's how memory sticks.

quiz.question: Why is spaced repetition effective?
options: Retrieval at the edge of forgetting strengthens memory
It eliminates the need for understanding

details.summary: Spaced repetition schedules reviews at increasing intervals, leveraging the spacing effect to maximize long-term retention with minimal study time. Reviewing material just before you would forget it strengthens the memory trace most efficiently. Apps like Anki automate optimal spacing schedules.
details.whyItMatters: Spaced repetition is the most evidence-backed technique for long-term memorization. It is dramatically more effective than massed practice or cramming.
takeaways: Reviews at expanding intervals maximize retention efficiency
The spacing effect is one of the most robust findings in learning
Automated systems calculate optimal review schedules

faq.question: How does spaced repetition differ from cramming?
faq.answer: Cramming masses all study into one session, producing strong short-term memory that fades quickly. Spaced repetition distributes practice across days or weeks, producing weaker initial performance but dramatically stronger long-term retention.

faq.question: What is the optimal spacing interval?
faq.answer: It depends on when you need to recall the information. A practical rule is to review after one day, then three days, then one week, then two weeks, expanding further. Adaptive algorithms in apps like Anki adjust intervals based on your actual performance for each item.
